bonuses.requirements: Trump to Emphasize Fight Against Overseas Crypto Fraud at White House EventHomeFeedNewsTrump to Emphasize Fight Against Overseas Crypto Fraud at White House EventTrump to Emphasize Fight Against Overseas Crypto Fraud at White House Event10/21 15:05U.S. President Trump will focus on his administration's efforts to combat overseas crypto fraud during a cybercrime prevention event at the White House on Wednesday. According to Reuters, citing White House officials, these overseas criminal networks lure Americans into fraudulent crypto investments. Trump, along with cabinet members, plans to highlight that the government has shut down multiple fake crypto investment websites and is working to close down online impersonation scams. Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin, FBI Director Kash Patel, Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth, and Attorney General Todd Blanche are expected to attend. This event follows an executive order issued in March of this year, where Trump instructed the Justice Department to prioritize identifying and prosecuting cyber fraudsters, followed by a memo requesting the Department of Homeland Security to collaborate with private companies to monitor foreign criminal hacker organizations. FBI data shows that in 2025, Americans submitted over 1 million complaints of online fraud, a 17% increase from 2024, resulting in record losses. Crypto fraud accounted for more than half of these losses, with the FBI's Internet Crime Complaint Center recording 181,565 crypto-related complaints, leading to losses of $11.366 billion, with $7.2 billion attributed to crypto investment scams. Most scams can be traced back to organized crime groups in Southeast Asia, involving Cambodia, Laos, and Myanmar, where criminals exploit trafficking victims as forced labor in scam operations. Americans aged 60 and above suffered the heaviest losses, with crypto-related losses reaching $4.43 billion. Crypto ATM scams caused losses of $389 million, a 58% increase from 2024; second

Bitcoin miners plunge up to 13% in Wall Street’s worst selloff since July | HTX InsightsHomeCrypto NewsBitcoin miners plunge up to 13...Bitcoin miners plunge up to 13% in Wall Street’s worst selloff since JulycointelegraphPublished on 2026-10-15Last updated on 2026-10-15AbstractU.S. stocks experienced their sharpest selloff since July, driven by hotter-than-expected inflation data. The S&P 500 fell 1.1%, and the Nasdaq Composite dropped 1.9%. Technology and AI infrastructure stocks were notably hit, with Bitcoin miners plunging as much as 13%. Companies like CoreWeave, Nebius, and Oracle saw significant declines.

The selloff extended to Bitcoin mining firms, many of which have expanded into AI infrastructure. TeraWulf, Core Scientific, Cipher Mining, and IREN all dropped over 12%. The downturn is partly attributed to concerns that higher interest rates could increase borrowing costs for data center expansion.

September's U.S. consumer prices rose 3.7% year-over-year, exceeding forecasts and the Fed's 2% target, largely due to higher gasoline prices. This data briefly boosted expectations for an October Fed rate hike, though San Francisco Fed President Mary Daly indicated there was no urgency to act immediately.#AI#Bitcoin#CPI#Fed#Inflation#Infrastructure#Miners#Selloff#Stocks#TechnologyUS stocks suffered their sharpest selloff since July on Wednesday as hotter-than-expected inflation data weighed on technology and AI infrastructure companies, with Bitcoin miners among those hit. The S&P 500 fell 1.1%, its biggest one-day decline since July 29; the Nasdaq Composite fell 1.9%, its biggest one-day drop since July 23, while the Dow Jones Industrial Average fell 0.1% over the day. Leading decliners among major tech companies included data center operator CoreWeave, which fell 16%, AI infrastructure provider Nebius, which fell 11%, and Oracle, which fell 9%. bonuses.requirements: NGRAVE Phishing Attack: Approximately 70 Wallets Stolen, $2.56 Million LostHomeFeedNewsNGRAVE Phishing Attack: Approximately 70 Wallets Stolen, $2.56 Million LostNGRAVE Phishing Attack: Approximately 70 Wallets Stolen, $2.56 Million Lost10/20 23:40Digital hardware wallet manufacturer NGRAVE disclosed that attackers hijacked a third-party notification service used by its LIQUID companion app, sending false security alerts to users, which led to the theft of approximately $2.56 million from around 70 wallet addresses across four blockchains. The losses included about $1.77 million in Bitcoin, approximately $454,000 in XRP, around $316,000 in Ethereum assets, and about $18,000 in Stellar. The attackers induced users to click on a phishing website and enter their 24-word recovery phrase or Perfect Key, subsequently using automated scripts to transfer assets within minutes. NGRAVE stated that the ZERO hardware wallet and private keys were not directly compromised; victims voluntarily provided their recovery credentials during the phishing process. Unauthorized access may have begun on October 11. After obtaining an access key, the attackers gained access to a broader key and sent false notifications on October 17; NGRAVE detected anomalies about one minute after the notifications appeared, but the first wallet was emptied six minutes later, and the notification system was shut down that evening. The CEO of NGRAVE stated that the company failed to fulfill the most basic security responsibilities of a cryptocurrency security firm and mentioned that affected keys have been replaced, with new dual approval, domain restrictions, and emergency shutdown mechanisms implemented. The company also advised affected users to create new wallets and contact the support team, noting that some device information, wallet activity, IP addresses, and approximate locations may have been exposed.BullishBearishLikeShareDisclaimer：The content above does not represent HTX's positions.，HTX does n

bonuses.requirements: EU authorities recognize Circle's USDC as 'significant' under MiCA | HTX InsightsHomeCrypto NewsIndepth ResearchEU authorities recognize Circl...EU authorities recognize Circle's USDC as 'significant' under MiCAcryptonews.ruPublished on 2026-10-14Last updated on 2026-10-14AbstractThe European Banking Authority (EBA) has classified Circle's USDC stablecoin as a "significant" electronic money token under the EU's Markets in Crypto-Assets (MiCA) regulation. This designation, shared by only 45 other projects, subjects USDC to joint oversight by the EBA and France's Autorité de Contrôle Prudentiel et de Résolution. As the world's second-largest stablecoin with a $73 billion market capitalization, USDC's new status comes amid EU-based issuers seeking regulated dollar-pegged stablecoins in the region. While European regulators cannot eliminate such dollar-linked tokens, they can enforce protective measures and rules for their issuers.#USDC Price#USDC Regular Invest#USDC Surge#USDC Plunge#Classification#electronic money#EU#European Banking Authority#Market Cap#MiCA#Regulation#Stablecoin#Supervision#USDCThe European Banking Authority (EBA) has classified the $USDC stablecoin from Circle as a significant electronic money token under the European Markets in Crypto-Assets (MiCA) legislation.In a notice published on Wednesday, the banking regulator stated that the electronic money token classification, granted to only 45 other projects, effectively means the $USDC stablecoin will be under the joint supervision of the EBA and the French supervisory authority — the Autorité de Contrôle Prudentiel et de Résolution. The stablecoin ranks second in market capitalization: $73 billion versus $184 billion for Tether USDt.The 'significant' status comes at a time when many EU-based token issuers have been striving for regulated, dollar-pegged stablecoins in the region.
